nodes.label: Apple Design Principles
nodes.rationale: The core interaction of area definition and photo positioning is pure direct manipulation. Springs, 1:1 pointer tracking, and rubber-banding make it feel physical.

nodes.label: Synthetic Email Pattern
nodes.rationale: Better Auth requires an email column but OpenFrame never asks for one. Server generates a synthetic <username>@openframe.local address that is never displayed or used.

nodes.label: Relative Coordinates
nodes.rationale: Slots stored as percentages (0-100) are resolution-independent and work across 1x, 2x, 3x outputs and different frame dimensions.

nodes.label: Client-Side Compositing
nodes.rationale: Frame PNG is already public. Client compositing strengthens privacy (P1) since participant photos never leave the browser.

nodes.label: Fabric.js (Rejected)
nodes.rationale: ~300KB canvas library for drag/resize of rectangles. SVG <rect> with pointer events achieves the same in ~150 lines with zero dependencies and precise 1:1 pointer tracking compatible with spring animations.

nodes.label: Privacy as Product Position (P1)
nodes.rationale: Privacy is a product-level position, not a feature checkbox. No email, no phone, participant photos never touch server.

nodes.label: Single Coordinate Path (P2)
nodes.rationale: Creator and participant must share the same coordinate geometry module. Two coordinate implementations mean two chances to be out of sync.

nodes.label: Single Compositing Path (P3)
nodes.rationale: Preview and download are produced by the same function at different scales. A preview that differs from the download is a class of bug eliminated by construction.

nodes.label: YAGNI (P4)
nodes.rationale: Every table, column, endpoint, and dependency must be justified by a real MVP feature.

nodes.label: Vite and Bun Split
nodes.rationale: Vite is the bundler/dev server (bundled with TanStack Start). Bun is the runtime, package manager, and test runner. They coexist without conflict.
